sources.claim: Checked 2026-10-20: 5.2.18 is the current 5.2 LTS patch, supported through April 2028; it is not the latest overall Django release.
Checked 2026-10-20: 17.11 is the current supported PostgreSQL 17 minor; major 17 support ends November 8, 2029.
Django 5.2 supports PostgreSQL 14+ and requires psycopg 3.1.8+ or psycopg2 2.8.4+. PostgreSQL 17 is a compatible proposal.

Django 5.2 supports Python 3.10 through 3.14 (3.14 added in 5.2.8), with supported latest micro releases. The document explicitly defers choosing and locking Python and the driver until authorized app setup; their absence is not an installed-runtime claim.
Explicit atomic blocks can commit or roll back linked payment and ledger writes together; this establishes feasibility, not correctness of an unimplemented command.

PostgreSQL supports row locking through select_for_update inside transactions. Meaningful concurrency verification must use PostgreSQL and TransactionTestCase rather than rely on SQLite or automatically wrapped TestCase transactions.
Django supplies CSRF middleware and form protection including login CSRF. Native JavaScript requests must carry the token and unsafe state changes must not be GET requests.
Django supports server-side sessions; signed-cookie session replay is not invalidated by logout, which motivates the session-backend finding.

The web manifest standard defines web-app identity, icons and standalone display; it does not require a frontend framework, so server-generated HTML with native JavaScript remains a feasible PWA approach.

Service workers and Cache API are web-platform capabilities. A deliberate public-assets-only cache policy is compatible with online-only private operations; no application or browser verification has occurred.

Supporting browser installation requires a manifest and HTTPS or local development origin; installation behavior differs across browsers. Used as supplementary browser guidance alongside primary W3C standards.

limitations: Independent draft technology review only; no human design acceptance, implementation authorization, production approval or successful app tests are implied.
Local _bmad/_config/manifest.yaml confirms core and bmm 6.12.4 installation. It does not attest Django, PostgreSQL, Docker, Python app runtime or driver installation.

Docker is an explicitly proposed deployment approach, not a selected installed release; hosting, mail delivery, concrete runtime versions, supported browser matrix and operational recovery/retention targets remain deferred with pre-build or pre-launch gates.
No infrastructure/provider selection, provisioning, dependency installation, secrets access or application changes were performed.

findings.issue: AD-3 specifies session cookie flags but leaves the session backend and server-side logout invalidation silent. Django's signed-cookie sessions do not invalidate a copied session on logout. Two implementations can therefore satisfy the written cookie flags while providing materially different logout protection for private household data.
findings.fix: Bind identity to server-side sessions (the existing PostgreSQL database is sufficient), require session rotation after code verification and server-side invalidation on logout, and prohibit financial data or OTP secrets in session cookies. This is a proposed architecture rule, not dependency installation or implementation approval.

reviewHistory.recheck: Independently reread current AD-3 on 2026-10-20. It now requires PostgreSQL-backed Django sessions, opaque session-ID cookies, rotation following code verification, server-side invalidation plus cookie deletion on logout, and expressly excludes signed-cookie sessions. The original medium finding is resolved at the draft contract level. Runtime enforcement and replay tests remain future implementation evidence.

initialFindings.issue: AD-10's withdrawal/deposit formula contradicts its no-new-headroom cycle invariant. With a 1,000 NOK monthly plan, no deposits and opening goal balance 100, S=1,000. Withdraw 100 and redeposit 100 in the same month: goal balance is restored, S remains 1,000, but W=100 permanently increases A by 100. The savings service can correctly record both transactions while the calculation service correctly applies the written formula and manufactures headroom.
initialFindings.fix: Define one explicit treatment for redeposits of released goal money, including within-plan deposits, and amend W/S together so a completed withdrawal/redeposit cycle restores A. Add this exact scenario alongside an ordinary withdrawal and a deposit exceeding plan. Keep the resulting rule proposed for human acceptance.

initialFindings.issue: AD-5 binds all history and defines historical cash result as I minus E minus actual deposits, but AD-10 excludes debt and annual-fund payments from E and adds W separately. A reporting unit obeying AD-5 omits actual debt/fund outflows and savings withdrawals; a ledger unit obeying AD-10 correctly classifies them separately. The same year therefore reports different cash result depending on which contract is followed. AD-10 calls A an extended formula but never supersedes the historical cash-result definition.
initialFindings.fix: Explicitly scope AD-5's simple A formula to the core projection and make AD-10 the authoritative expanded calculation. Define the signed historical cash-result projection across every actual posting class, including refunds and withdrawals, separately from allocations/reservations; include an example with a fund-funded payment and debt payment. Update the capability map's reporting references.

initialFindings.issue: AD-6 requires every paid occurrence to create one linked expense and puts paid bills in category consumption (AD-5), while AD-10 requires linked debt/fund occurrences to point to their single non-E-class posting. A generic bills implementation can obey AD-6 by creating an ordinary expense, while debt/fund modules obey AD-10 by creating their own payment, resulting in two effects or a class conflict. The exception and dispatch ownership are not expressed in the shared payment command contract.
initialFindings.fix: State that the bill payment command creates exactly one posting whose class comes from the occurrence's ordinary/debt/fund obligation type; ordinary postings alone enter E, with debt/fund settlement delegated atomically to their respective rules. Define whether category actuals include each class, and apply the same dispatch to undo/refund without creating a second posting.

initialFindings.issue: AD-4 permits historical effective-date corrections and AD-10 allows withdrawal up to available goal balance, but it does not define available balance as of the withdrawal date or the validity of later events after correction. A goal service can check today's balance under a lock and accept a September withdrawal against an October deposit; a historical reporting service then reconstructs a negative September goal balance while still obeying the date rules. The dated opening balance creates the same seam if used before its effective date.
initialFindings.fix: Specify an effective-date balance rule for withdrawals/opening balances and a minimal rule for later withdrawals made invalid by editing/deleting earlier funding. Validate the affected chronological goal history atomically, or explicitly prohibit those mutations until a correction flow is agreed; add one backdated withdrawal example.
